title: Crazyflie connection protocol
description: Version 1. The messages between the Crazyflie connection server and its clients, each one JSON text frame on a WebSocket. Generated from crates/protocol/src/lib.rs

Scan all channels for Crazyflies at an address. Refused while a job runs

address.description: 10 hex digits, E7E7E7E7E7 when not given

oneOf.description: Check which of these Crazyflies answer, one packet each, without connecting. Connected ones answer without radio traffic
List the Crazyflies the server is connected to
Attach to a Crazyflie, connecting it if no other client has
Detach from a Crazyflie. It is disconnected a while (the server's linger time) after its last client detaches
Read a param from the Crazyflie
Set a param. Every value is a number, converted to the param's type
Stream of `param_changed` event for every param set by any client
Whether a param can be stored in the EEPROM. Replies `bool` reply. Asks the Crazyflie, so it isn't part of `AttachInfo`

Store the current value of a persistent param in the Crazyflie's EEPROM
Clear the stored value of a persistent param
Stream of `log` event with the given variables. Variables that don't fit one log block (26 bytes) are spread over several, each arriving as its own event
Stream of `console` event lines

oneOf.description: Arm or disarm the motors
Stop the motors at once. The Crazyflie has to be restarted to fly again
Recover a Crazyflie that crashed (tumbled)
The radio link's statistics

Restart the Crazyflies into their bootloaders, flash the images to each and restart them into their firmware, as a job on stream `sub`: `progress` event, one `flashed` event or `flash_failed` event per Crazyflie, then `done` event. The images are for one platform. The Crazyflies whose bootloaders take broadcast get each image at the same time, the others one after another. Clients attached to them are disconnected, and attaching and scanning are refused until the job is done. The job finishes even if the client that started it goes away
Stream of `busy` event and `available` event: the Crazyflies that jobs take over and give back

Write `data` to memory `id` at `address`
Read a deck's 1-wire memory `id`: its ids and elements (board name, revision, …)
Read the EEPROM config memory `id`
Write the EEPROM config memory `id`. The firmware applies it at boot
Read the geometry of base station `bs` from lighthouse memory `id`
Write the geometry of base station `bs` to lighthouse memory `id`. The Crazyflie uses it until it restarts, see `lighthouse_persist`
Read the calibration of base station `bs` from lighthouse memory `id`
Write the calibration of base station `bs` to lighthouse memory `id`. The Crazyflie uses it until it restarts, see `lighthouse_persist`
Write uncompressed trajectory segments to trajectory memory `id` at `start_addr`. Replies `written` reply
Write a compressed trajectory to trajectory memory `id` at `start_addr`. Replies `written` reply
The anchor ids in Loco memory `id`: all configured ones, or the `active` ones. Replies `ids` reply
The position of `anchor` in Loco memory `id`
Send a Loco Positioning Protocol packet to anchor `dest_id`, through the Crazyflie (e.g. an anchor position)
Store the geometries and calibrations of these base stations in the Crazyflie's flash. Replies `bool` reply: whether the Crazyflie did

geometries.description: Base stations whose geometry to store

calibrations.description: Base stations whose calibration to store

oneOf.description: A command the Crazyflie's nRF51 handles, sent without connecting to it. Its clients are disconnected, except by `power_on_stm32_domain`. Fails if it doesn't answer

new_uri.description: With `reboot`, where the Crazyflie comes back when its radio channel or address was changed in its EEPROM config: the reply waits for its firmware there, it isn't connected again, and `available` event says where it moved

id.description: Picked by the client, echoed in the reply

oneOf.description: Answer to the request with the same `id`. Exactly one of `ok` and `error` is set
Data on a stream opened by the client with `sub`
A Crazyflie this client is attached to was disconnected

start.description: Where to write the image; the start of the firmware area when not given

LighthouseBsGeometry.description: Where a lighthouse base station is, see `crazyflie_lib::subsystems::memory::LighthouseBsGeometry`

LighthouseBsCalibration.description: A lighthouse base station's calibration, see `crazyflie_lib::subsystems::memory::LighthouseBsCalibration`

LighthouseCalibrationSweep.description: The calibration of one of a base station's two sweeps, see `crazyflie_lib::subsystems::memory::LighthouseCalibrationSweep`

Poly.description: A polynomial of up to 8 coefficients, see `crazyflie_lib::subsystems::memory::Poly`

CompressedStart.description: Where a compressed trajectory starts, see `crazyflie_lib::subsystems::memory::CompressedStart`

CompressedSegment.description: A compressed trajectory segment: the Bézier control points of each axis, 0, 1, 3 or 7 of them, see `crazyflie_lib::subsystems::memory::CompressedSegment`

PlatformCommand.description: Commands for `platform`, named after the crazyflie-lib functions

oneOf.description: Restart the firmware. The reply comes once the firmware answers again; meanwhile the Crazyflie is busy (`busy` event), and a client that was attached gets it back connected (`available` event)
Power off the whole Crazyflie, as the power button does. Only the button turns it on again
Power off the STM32 and decks (sleep). The nRF51 stays on the radio. The Crazyflie is announced busy, and attaching fails until it is woken up
Power the STM32 and decks on again (wake up). The reply comes once the firmware answers; the Crazyflie is then announced available
Done, nothing to return

radio_send_rate.description: Packets sent per second, with the empty ones

power_detector_rate.description: Share of acks where the nRF24 power detector triggered, 0 to 1

rssi.description: dBm, measured by the Crazyradio on acks

used_pins.description: Bitmask of the deck pins the deck uses
